source.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα χωρισθεὶς ἐκ τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ἦλθεν εἰς Κόρινθον.

records.literal_gloss: After these things having departed from the Athens he came to Corinth.

en.L: After these things, having left Athens, he came to Corinth.
en.B: After this, Paul left Athens and went on to Corinth.
en.R: After this, Paul left the city of Athens and went to the city of Corinth.

es.L: Después de estas cosas, saliendo de Atenas, fue a Corinto.
es.B: Después de esto, Pablo salió de Atenas y siguió hasta Corinto.
es.R: Después de esto, Pablo salió de la ciudad de Atenas y fue a la ciudad de Corinto.

fr.L: Après cela, ayant quitté Athènes, il vint à Corinthe.
fr.B: Après cela, Paul quitta Athènes et se rendit à Corinthe.
fr.R: Ensuite, Paul a quitté la ville d’Athènes et il est allé dans la ville de Corinthe.

sw.L: Baada ya mambo haya, akiisha kuondoka Athene, alifika Korintho.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Paulo aliondoka Athene, akaenda Korintho.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Paulo aliuacha mji wa Athene, akaenda mji wa Korintho.

vi.L: Sau những việc ấy, ông rời A-thên và đến Cô-rinh-tô.
vi.B: Sau đó, Phao-lô rời A-thên và đi đến Cô-rinh-tô.
vi.R: Sau việc đó, Phao-lô rời thành A-thên và đi đến thành Cô-rinh-tô.

ko.L: 이 일들 뒤에 그는 아덴을 떠나 고린도로 갔다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 바울은 아덴을 떠나 고린도로 갔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 바울은 아덴을 떠나 고린도라는 도시로 갔다.

pt.L: Depois destas coisas, tendo saído de Atenas, ele chegou a Corinto.
pt.B: Depois disso, Paulo saiu de Atenas e foi para Corinto.
pt.R: Depois disso, Paulo saiu da cidade de Atenas e foi para a cidade de Corinto.

am.L: ከዚህ በኋላ ከአቴና ተለይቶ ወደ ቆሮንቶስ መጣ።
am.B: ከዚህ በኋላ ጳውሎስ ከአቴና ተነሥቶ ወደ ቆሮንቶስ ሄደ።
am.R: ከዚህ በኋላ ጳውሎስ የአቴናን ከተማ ትቶ ወደ ቆሮንቶስ ከተማ ሄደ።

hi.L: इन बातों के बाद वह एथेंस को छोड़कर कुरिन्थुस में आया।
hi.B: इसके बाद पौलुस एथेंस से निकलकर कुरिन्थुस पहुँचा।
hi.R: इसके बाद पौलुस एथेंस शहर से चलकर कुरिन्थुस शहर में गया।

ru.L: После этого, оставив Афины, он пришёл в Коринф.
ru.B: После этого Павел покинул Афины и отправился в Коринф.
ru.R: После этого Павел ушёл из города Афины и пришёл в город Коринф.

uk.L: Після цього, покинувши Афіни, він прийшов до Коринта.
uk.B: Після цього Павло залишив Афіни і пішов до Коринта.
uk.R: Після цього Павло залишив місто Афіни і пішов до міста Коринта.

ja.L: これらのことの後、アテネを離れて、コリントに来た。
ja.B: その後、パウロはアテネを去ってコリントへ行った。
ja.R: そのあと、パウロはアテネの町を出て、コリントの町へ行きました。

decisions.choice: Corinth: the leading city of the province of Achaia
decisions.reason: Corinth stood on the narrow neck of land between mainland Greece and the Peloponnese, with a port on each sea (Cenchreae, 18:18, was the eastern one). Rome destroyed the old city in 146 BC, and Julius Caesar refounded it as a Roman colony in 44 BC. It was the seat of the proconsul of Achaia (18:12).

decisions.choice: he: Paul, who had been in Athens (17:16-34)
decisions.reason: Paul was alone in Athens; Silas and Timothy join him later (18:5).

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Paul at the start of a new chapter and a new place.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As for the whole book (1:3): the passé simple is the tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Greek imperfects ("il discutait", "ils croyaient") stay imperfects. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: "Cô-rinh-tô" for Corinth
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration, as in 2 Timothy 4:20.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Acts 18; God and the Lord take the honorific in the narrative and in speech; the Lord speaks to Paul in 해라체, as Jesus speaks in the Korean Gospels
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters (style guide, section 7). "고린도" is the Protestant form of Corinth, as in the Korean 2 Timothy 4:20.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns and verb endings for the Lord in this chapter are written once, with no span.

decisions.choice: አቴና (Athens), ቆሮንቶስ (Corinth)
decisions.reason: Names of places in Acts keep the forms long used in Amharic Bibles and church speech, so readers recognise them; አቴንስ is how the modern city is named in the news, but it would sound out of place in the story.

source.text: καὶ εὑρών τινα Ἰουδαῖον ὀνόματι Ἀκύλαν, Ποντικὸν τῷ γένει, προσφάτως ἐληλυθότα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸ διατεταχέναι Κλαύδιον χωρίζεσθαι πάντας τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥώμης, προσῆλθεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ διὰ τὸ ὁμότεχνον εἶναι ἔμενεν παρ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἠργάζετο, ἦσαν γὰρ σκηνοποιοὶ τῇ τέχνῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And having found a certain Jew by name Aquila, of Pontus by the birth, recently having come from the Italy, and Priscilla wife of him, because of the having commanded Claudius to depart all the Jews from the Rome, he came to them, \v 3 and because of the same trade to be he stayed with them and worked; they were for tentmakers by the trade.

en.L: And having found a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome, he went to them, \v 3 and because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked; for they were tentmakers by trade.
en.B: There he met a Jew called Aquila, born in Pontus, who had lately arrived from Italy with his wife Priscilla, since Claudius had ordered every Jew to leave Rome. Paul went to see them, \v 3 and because he and they worked at the same craft, he stayed in their home and worked with them. By trade they were tentmakers.
en.R: In Corinth Paul met a Jew named Aquila. He came from Pontus, but he and his wife Priscilla had recently come to Corinth from Italy. They left Italy because the emperor Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave the city of Rome. Paul went to visit them. \v 3 They did the same kind of work as Paul: they made tents. So Paul stayed with them and worked with them.

es.L: Y habiendo encontrado a un judío llamado Aquila, natural del Ponto, recién llegado de Italia, y a Priscila su mujer, porque Claudio había ordenado que todos los judíos salieran de Roma, fue a ellos, \v 3 y como era del mismo oficio, se quedó con ellos y trabajaba; porque eran fabricantes de tiendas de oficio.
es.B: Allí conoció a un judío llamado Aquila, nacido en el Ponto, que acababa de llegar de Italia con su esposa Priscila, porque Claudio había ordenado que todos los judíos salieran de Roma. Pablo fue a verlos, \v 3 y como tenían el mismo oficio, se quedó en su casa y trabajaba con ellos. Eran fabricantes de tiendas de campaña.
es.R: En Corinto, Pablo conoció a un judío llamado Aquila. Era del Ponto, pero él y su esposa Priscila habían llegado hacía poco a Corinto desde Italia. Habían salido de Italia porque el emperador Claudio había ordenado a todos los judíos que salieran de la ciudad de Roma. Pablo fue a visitarlos. \v 3 Ellos hacían el mismo trabajo que Pablo: fabricaban tiendas de campaña. Así que Pablo se quedó con ellos y trabajó con ellos.

fr.L: Et ayant trouvé un Juif nommé Aquilas, originaire du Pont, récemment arrivé d’Italie, ainsi que Priscille, sa femme, parce que Claude avait ordonné que tous les Juifs quittent Rome, il alla vers eux, \v 3 et, parce qu’il était du même métier, il logeait chez eux et travaillait ; car ils étaient fabricants de tentes de métier.
fr.B: Il y fit la connaissance d’un Juif nommé Aquilas, né dans le Pont, qui venait d’arriver d’Italie avec sa femme Priscille, parce que Claude avait ordonné à tous les Juifs de quitter Rome. Paul alla les voir \v 3 et, comme il exerçait le même métier qu’eux, il logea chez eux et travailla avec eux. Leur métier était de fabriquer des tentes.
fr.R: À Corinthe, Paul a rencontré un Juif appelé Aquilas. Il venait de la région du Pont, mais lui et sa femme Priscille venaient d’arriver d’Italie à Corinthe. Ils avaient quitté l’Italie parce que l’empereur Claude avait ordonné à tous les Juifs de quitter la ville de Rome. Paul est allé leur rendre visite. \v 3 Ils faisaient le même travail que Paul : ils fabriquaient des tentes. Alors Paul est resté chez eux et il a travaillé avec eux.

sw.L: Na akiisha kumkuta Myahudi mmoja jina lake Akila, mzaliwa wa Ponto, aliyekuwa amekuja karibuni kutoka Italia, pamoja na Prisila mke wake, kwa sababu Klaudio alikuwa ameamuru Wayahudi wote waondoke Roma, alikwenda kwao, \v 3 na kwa kuwa walikuwa na kazi moja, alikaa kwao akafanya kazi; kwa maana kazi yao ilikuwa kushona mahema.
sw.B: Huko alimkuta Myahudi mmoja aitwaye Akila, mzaliwa wa Ponto, ambaye alikuwa amewasili karibuni kutoka Italia pamoja na mke wake Prisila, kwa kuwa Klaudio alikuwa ameamuru kila Myahudi aondoke Roma. Paulo alikwenda kuwaona, \v 3 na kwa sababu yeye na wao walikuwa na ufundi mmoja, alikaa nyumbani kwao, akafanya kazi pamoja nao. Kazi yao ilikuwa kushona mahema.
sw.R: Huko Korintho Paulo alikutana na Myahudi mmoja aitwaye Akila. Akila alitoka Ponto, lakini yeye na mke wake Prisila walikuwa wamefika Korintho karibuni kutoka Italia. Waliondoka Italia kwa sababu mfalme Klaudio alikuwa ameamuru Wayahudi wote waondoke mji wa Roma. Paulo alikwenda kuwatembelea. \v 3 Walifanya kazi ileile kama Paulo: walishona mahema. Kwa hiyo Paulo alikaa kwao, akafanya kazi pamoja nao.

vi.L: Và gặp một người Do Thái tên là A-qui-la, quê ở Bông, mới từ Y-ta-li đến cùng với Bê-rít-sin, vợ ông, vì Cơ-lốt đã ra lệnh cho mọi người Do Thái phải rời khỏi Rô-ma, ông đến với họ, \v 3 và vì cùng làm một nghề, ông ở lại với họ và làm việc; vì nghề của họ là may lều.
vi.B: Ở đó ông gặp một người Do Thái tên là A-qui-la, sinh ở Bông, mới cùng vợ là Bê-rít-sin từ Y-ta-li đến, vì Cơ-lốt đã ra lệnh cho mọi người Do Thái phải rời khỏi Rô-ma. Phao-lô đến thăm họ, \v 3 và vì cùng làm một nghề, ông ở lại nhà họ và làm việc với họ. Nghề của họ là may lều.
vi.R: Ở Cô-rinh-tô, Phao-lô gặp một người Do Thái tên là A-qui-la. Ông quê ở Bông, nhưng ông và vợ là Bê-rít-sin mới từ Y-ta-li đến Cô-rinh-tô. Họ rời Y-ta-li vì hoàng đế Cơ-lốt đã ra lệnh cho mọi người Do Thái phải rời khỏi thành Rô-ma. Phao-lô đến thăm họ. \v 3 Họ làm cùng một nghề với Phao-lô: họ may lều. Vì vậy Phao-lô ở lại nhà họ và làm việc với họ.

ko.L: 그리고 [그곳에서] 아굴라라는 어떤 유대인을 만났다. 그는 본도 태생으로, 글라우디오가 모든 유대인에게 로마를 떠나라고 명령했기 때문에, 그의 아내 브리스길라와 함께 이탈리아에서 최근에 온 사람이었다. 바울은 그들에게 찾아갔다. \v 3 그리고 직업이 같았으므로 그들과 함께 지내며 일하였다. 그들의 직업은 천막을 만드는 일이었다.
ko.B: 그곳에서 바울은 아굴라라는 유대인을 만났다. 그는 본도에서 태어났는데, 글라우디오가 모든 유대인에게 로마를 떠나라고 명령했기 때문에 얼마 전에 아내 브리스길라와 함께 이탈리아에서 온 사람이었다. 바울은 그들을 찾아갔다. \v 3 바울은 그들과 같은 일을 하는 사람이었으므로, 그들의 집에 머물면서 함께 일했다. 그들의 직업은 천막을 만드는 일이었다.
ko.R: 고린도에서 바울은 아굴라라는 유대인을 만났다. 아굴라는 본도 출신이었지만, 얼마 전에 아내 브리스길라와 함께 이탈리아에서 고린도로 왔다. 로마 황제 글라우디오가 모든 유대인에게 로마를 떠나라고 명령했기 때문에 이탈리아를 떠난 것이었다. 바울은 그들을 찾아갔다. \v 3 그들은 바울과 같은 일을 했다. 그들은 천막을 만드는 사람들이었다. 그래서 바울은 그들의 집에 머물면서 함께 일했다.

pt.L: E, tendo encontrado um certo judeu chamado Áquila, natural do Ponto, que tinha chegado recentemente da Itália, e Priscila, sua mulher, porque Cláudio tinha ordenado que todos os judeus saíssem de Roma, foi até eles \v 3 e, por ser do mesmo ofício, ficou com eles e trabalhava; pois eram fabricantes de tendas de ofício.
pt.B: Ali ele conheceu um judeu chamado Áquila, nascido no Ponto, que tinha chegado havia pouco da Itália com a sua mulher, Priscila, pois Cláudio tinha ordenado que todos os judeus saíssem de Roma. Paulo foi visitá-los \v 3 e, como ele e eles tinham o mesmo ofício, ficou morando com eles e trabalhando com eles. Eram fabricantes de tendas.
pt.R: Em Corinto, Paulo conheceu um judeu chamado Áquila. Ele era do Ponto, mas ele e a sua esposa, Priscila, tinham chegado havia pouco tempo da Itália. Eles saíram da Itália porque o imperador Cláudio tinha mandado que todos os judeus saíssem da cidade de Roma. Paulo foi visitá-los. \v 3 Eles faziam o mesmo tipo de trabalho que Paulo: fabricavam tendas. Por isso Paulo ficou com eles e trabalhou com eles.

am.L: በትውልዱ የጳንጦስ ሰው የሆነ፣ ቀላውዴዎስ አይሁድ ሁሉ ከሮም እንዲወጡ ስላዘዘ ከኢጣሊያ በቅርቡ የመጣ አቂላ የሚባል አንድ አይሁዳዊና ሚስቱን ጵርስቅላን አግኝቶ ወደ እነርሱ ሄደ፤ \v 3 ሙያቸውም አንድ ስለ ነበረ ከእነርሱ ጋር ተቀምጦ ይሠራ ነበር፤ በሙያቸው ድንኳን ሰፊዎች ነበሩና።
am.B: በዚያም በትውልዱ የጳንጦስ ሰው የሆነ አቂላ የሚባል አንድ አይሁዳዊ አገኘ። እርሱም ቀላውዴዎስ አይሁድ ሁሉ ሮምን ለቀው እንዲወጡ ስላዘዘ ከሚስቱ ከጵርስቅላ ጋር ከኢጣሊያ በቅርቡ መጥቶ ነበር። ጳውሎስም ሊጠይቃቸው ሄደ፤ \v 3 ሙያቸው አንድ ስለ ነበረም በቤታቸው ተቀምጦ አብሯቸው ይሠራ ነበር። በሙያቸው ድንኳን ሰፊዎች ነበሩ።
am.R: ጳውሎስ በቆሮንቶስ አቂላ የሚባል አንድ አይሁዳዊ አገኘ። አቂላ የጳንጦስ ሰው ነበር፤ ነገር ግን እርሱና ሚስቱ ጵርስቅላ በቅርቡ ከኢጣሊያ ወደ ቆሮንቶስ መጥተው ነበር። ኢጣሊያን የለቀቁት ንጉሠ ነገሥቱ ቀላውዴዎስ አይሁድ ሁሉ ከሮም ከተማ እንዲወጡ ስላዘዘ ነው። ጳውሎስ ሊጠይቃቸው ሄደ። \v 3 እነርሱም እንደ ጳውሎስ ያለ ሥራ ይሠሩ ነበር፤ ድንኳን ይሰፉ ነበር። ስለዚህ ጳውሎስ ከእነርሱ ጋር ተቀምጦ አብሯቸው ሠራ።

hi.L: और वहाँ अक्विला नाम का एक यहूदी मिला, जिसका जन्म पुन्तुस में हुआ था, और जो हाल ही में अपनी पत्नी प्रिस्किल्ला के साथ इतालिया से आया था, क्योंकि क्लौदियुस ने सब यहूदियों को रोम से निकल जाने की आज्ञा दी थी; वह उनके पास गया, \v 3 और एक ही धंधा होने के कारण वह उनके साथ रहा और काम करता रहा; क्योंकि उनका धंधा तंबू बनाना था।
hi.B: वहाँ उसे अक्विला नाम का एक यहूदी मिला, जिसका जन्म पुन्तुस में हुआ था। वह हाल ही में अपनी पत्नी प्रिस्किल्ला के साथ इतालिया से आया था, क्योंकि क्लौदियुस ने आज्ञा दी थी कि सब यहूदी रोम छोड़ दें। पौलुस उनसे मिलने गया, \v 3 और क्योंकि उसका और उनका एक ही धंधा था, वह उनके घर में रहकर उनके साथ काम करने लगा। उनका धंधा तंबू बनाना था।
hi.R: कुरिन्थुस में पौलुस को अक्विला नाम का एक यहूदी मिला। वह पुन्तुस का रहनेवाला था, पर वह और उसकी पत्नी प्रिस्किल्ला हाल ही में इतालिया से कुरिन्थुस आए थे। उन्होंने इतालिया इसलिए छोड़ा था क्योंकि सम्राट क्लौदियुस ने सब यहूदियों को रोम शहर छोड़ने की आज्ञा दी थी। पौलुस उनसे मिलने गया। \v 3 वे भी वही काम करते थे जो पौलुस करता था: वे तंबू बनाते थे। इसलिए पौलुस उनके साथ रहा और उनके साथ काम करने लगा।

ru.L: И, найдя некоего иудея по имени Акила, родом из Понта, недавно пришедшего из Италии, и Прискиллу, жену его, — потому что Клавдий повелел всем иудеям удалиться из Рима, — он пришёл к ним \v 3 и, так как был того же ремесла, остался у них и работал; ведь они по ремеслу были изготовителями палаток.
ru.B: Там он встретил иудея по имени Акила, родом из Понта, который недавно прибыл из Италии со своей женой Прискиллой, потому что Клавдий приказал всем иудеям покинуть Рим. Павел пошёл к ним \v 3 и, так как он и они занимались одним ремеслом, остался у них в доме и работал вместе с ними. По ремеслу они делали палатки.
ru.R: В Коринфе Павел встретил иудея по имени Акила. Он был родом из Понта, но они с женой Прискиллой недавно пришли в Коринф из Италии. Они уехали из Италии, потому что император Клавдий приказал всем иудеям покинуть город Рим. Павел пошёл навестить их. \v 3 Они занимались тем же делом, что и Павел: шили палатки. Поэтому Павел остался у них и работал вместе с ними.

uk.L: І, знайшовши одного юдея на імʼя Акила, родом з Понту, який нещодавно прийшов з Італії, і Прискиллу, його дружину, — бо Клавдій наказав усім юдеям вийти з Рима, — він прийшов до них, \v 3 і, оскільки був того самого ремесла, залишився в них і працював; бо вони були ремеслом наметники.
uk.B: Там він зустрів юдея на імʼя Акила, родом з Понту, який недавно прибув з Італії зі своєю дружиною Прискиллою, бо Клавдій наказав усім юдеям покинути Рим. Павло пішов до них \v 3 і, оскільки вони мали одне ремесло, залишився в їхньому домі й працював разом з ними. Ремеслом вони були наметники.
uk.R: У Коринті Павло зустрів юдея на імʼя Акила. Він був родом з Понту, але нещодавно разом зі своєю дружиною Прискиллою прийшов до Коринта з Італії. Вони покинули Італію, бо імператор Клавдій наказав усім юдеям вийти з міста Рима. Павло пішов до них у гості. \v 3 Вони робили ту саму роботу, що й Павло: шили намети. Тож Павло жив у них і працював разом з ними.

ja.L: そして、ポントス生まれで、最近イタリアから来たばかりのアキラという名のユダヤ人と、その妻プリスキラを見つけた。クラウディウスが、すべてのユダヤ人にローマから立ち去るよう命じていたからである。[パウロは]彼らのところに行った。\v 3 そして、同じ職業であったので、彼らのもとにとどまって働いた。彼らの職業はテント造りであった。
ja.B: そこでパウロは、ポントス生まれのアキラというユダヤ人に出会った。アキラは、クラウディウス帝がすべてのユダヤ人にローマからの退去を命じたため、妻のプリスキラと共に最近イタリアから来たばかりであった。パウロは二人を訪ね、\v 3 同じ仕事をしていたので、その家に住み込んで一緒に働いた。彼らの仕事はテント造りであった。
ja.R: コリントで、パウロはアキラというユダヤ人に会いました。アキラはポントスの出身でしたが、最近、妻のプリスキラと一緒にイタリアからコリントに来ていました。ローマ皇帝クラウディウスが、ユダヤ人は皆ローマの町から出て行くようにと命じたので、イタリアを離れたのです。パウロは二人を訪ねました。\v 3 二人はパウロと同じ仕事をしていました。テントを作る仕事です。それでパウロは二人の家に泊まり、一緒に働きました。

decisions.choice: Claudius's order sending the Jews out of Rome, probably about AD 49
alternatives: a date early in Claudius's reign, AD 41
decisions.reason: Claudius was emperor from AD 41 to 54. The Roman writer Suetonius (Claudius 25.4) says that Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome because they were constantly rioting at the prompting of "Chrestus", a form of the name Christ. The date AD 49 comes from the fifth-century writer Orosius, whose source is not known. Dio Cassius (60.6.6) speaks instead of a ban on Jewish meetings in AD 41, which some connect with the same events. So the year is not certain.

decisions.choice: all the Jews: the order as it was given, not a claim that every Jew left
alternatives: every Jew without exception left Rome
decisions.reason: Luke reports the terms of the order. Jews were living in Rome again a few years later: Priscilla and Aquila themselves were back there when Paul wrote Romans (Romans 16:3), and Paul meets the Jewish leaders of Rome in 28:17.

decisions.choice: Aquila and Priscilla: a Jewish couple from Pontus who had lived in Rome
alternatives: already leaders of the church in Rome
decisions.reason: Pontus was a region on the south coast of the Black Sea. The couple appear again in 18:18, 18:26, Romans 16:3, 1 Corinthians 16:19 and 2 Timothy 4:19, where Paul calls her Prisca, the shorter form of the name. Luke does not say whether they were already believers when Paul met them.

decisions.choice: tentmakers: people who made tents, perhaps leatherworkers more generally
decisions.reason: The word means a maker of tents. Tents were made of leather or of cloth woven from goat hair, so the trade may have been leatherwork of many kinds. The word itself does not settle which material they worked in.

decisions.choice: Paul worked with his hands to support himself
alternatives: he worked only to help the couple
decisions.reason: Paul says he earned his own living so as not to be a burden to the churches (20:34; 1 Corinthians 4:12; 9:6-15; 1 Thessalonians 2:9).

decisions.choice: the Greek order, close to other literal versions
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Greek sentence closely, so it will look like other word-for-word translations here.

decisions.choice: the emperor Claudius
decisions.reason: Readable says who Claudius was.

decisions.choice: Priscila
decisions.reason: Luke uses the longer, familiar form of her name, and Spanish keeps "Priscila" here and in verses 18 and 26; Paul's letters use the short form, "Prisca" (meaning decision m3 names the couple).

decisions.choice: Aquilas, Priscille (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: These are the usual French forms of the two names, as Claude is for Claudius and Gallion for Gallio (18:12).

decisions.choice: Akila, Prisila
decisions.reason: Luke uses the familiar form of her name, so "Prisila" here; Romans 16:3 has the short form "Priska", as Paul writes it. The same in 18:18 and 18:26.

decisions.choice: kushona mahema
decisions.reason: Tents were sewn from leather or cloth (meaning decision), so "kushona mahema" (to sew tents) says what the craft was; a footnote in the English notes that they may have been leatherworkers more generally.

decisions.choice: "A-qui-la" and "Bê-rít-sin"
decisions.reason: Acts calls her by the familiar form of her name, Priscilla; Paul's letters call her Prisca, "Bê-rít-ca" in Romans 16:3. The two forms are kept apart, as the Greek has them, and both are the same woman.

decisions.choice: "Bông", "Y-ta-li", "Cơ-lốt", "Rô-ma"
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliterations; "Bông" as in 1 Peter 1:1 and "Rô-ma" as in Romans 1:7.

decisions.choice: "아굴라", "브리스길라", "본도", "글라우디오" (with "로마 황제" at Readable), "이탈리아"
decisions.reason: Luke uses the longer form Priscilla, Paul the shorter Prisca, which the Korean Romans 16:3 gives as "브리스가"; Korean keeps the two forms apart as the Greek does. The names are the Protestant forms (style guide, Settled); for the country Korean uses the current name, as the Korean letters do for Egypt ("이집트").

decisions.choice: ድንኳን ሰፊዎች (tent-sewers), ድንኳን ይሰፉ ነበር (R)
decisions.reason: Tents were made by cutting and sewing leather or woven cloth, and Amharic speaks of a tent being sewn (ድንኳን መስፋት); ሠሪዎች is not wrong, but ሰፊዎች names the craft as a reader would know it.

decisions.choice: the descriptions of Aquila placed before his name, with the main verb at the end
decisions.reason: Amharic puts a relative clause before the noun it describes and the verb last, so Literal keeps the Greek's units (having found ... he went to them) but cannot keep their order.

decisions.choice: "अक्विला", "इतालिया", "प्रिस्किल्ला", "क्लौदियुस"
decisions.reason: The established Hindi Bible forms of the names, which keep the Greek sounds. Readable adds "सम्राट" to say who Claudius was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "палатки"
decisions.reason: The trade was making tents, perhaps of leather; "палатка" is the plain modern word.

decisions.choice: "ポントス", "イタリア", "クラウディウス" ("クラウディウス帝" B; "ローマ皇帝クラウディウス" R)
decisions.reason: Names not in the brief, in the forms closest to the Greek and Latin. Balanced and Readable say that Claudius was the emperor (m1).

decisions.choice: "テント造り" (L, B); "テントを作る仕事" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a maker of tents and does not say which material (m4). "テント" is the everyday word; "天幕" is older and less familiar.

source.text: διελέγετο δὲ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον, ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας.

records.literal_gloss: He was reasoning now in the synagogue on every Sabbath, persuading both Jews and Greeks.

en.L: And he was reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath and was persuading both Jews and Greeks.
en.B: Each Sabbath he debated in the synagogue, seeking to win over Jews and Greeks alike.
en.R: Every Sabbath day Paul went to the synagogue. He talked with the people there and tried to convince both Jews and Greeks to believe the message about Jesus.

es.L: Y discutía en la sinagoga cada sábado, y persuadía a judíos y a griegos.
es.B: Cada sábado debatía en la sinagoga, tratando de convencer tanto a judíos como a griegos.
es.R: Cada sábado Pablo iba a la sinagoga. Hablaba con la gente de allí y trataba de convencer a judíos y a griegos de que creyeran el mensaje acerca de Jesús.

fr.L: Et il discutait dans la synagogue chaque sabbat, et il persuadait Juifs et Grecs.
fr.B: Chaque sabbat, il discutait dans la synagogue, cherchant à convaincre Juifs et Grecs.
fr.R: Chaque jour de sabbat, Paul allait à la synagogue. Il parlait avec les gens qui étaient là et il essayait de convaincre les Juifs et les Grecs de croire au message sur Jésus.

vi.R: Mỗi ngày Sa-bát, Phao-lô đi đến nhà hội. Ông trò chuyện với những người ở đó và cố gắng thuyết phục cả người Do Thái lẫn người Hy Lạp tin sứ điệp về Đức Giê-xu.

pt.L: E ele discutia na sinagoga todos os sábados e persuadia tanto judeus como gregos.
pt.B: Todos os sábados ele debatia na sinagoga, procurando convencer tanto judeus como gregos.
pt.R: Todos os sábados Paulo ia à sinagoga. Ele conversava com as pessoas de lá e tentava convencer tanto judeus como gregos a acreditar na mensagem sobre Jesus.

am.L: በየሰንበቱም በምኩራብ ይከራከር ነበር፤ አይሁድንና ግሪኮችንም ያሳምን ነበር።
am.B: በየሰንበቱ በምኩራብ እየተከራከረ አይሁድንም ግሪኮችንም ለማሳመን ይጥር ነበር።
